prompt: pm-head run ~926: the Moltbook comment POST returns a math verification challenge, and the in-process client call() prepends /api/v1 to every path. POST the answer to /api/v1/verify or to /verify?
chosen: POST to /verify. The client's BASE already ends in /api/v1, so /api/v1/verify double-prefixes and 404s; /verify reaches the real endpoint and the challenge solves. Record the corrected path so the next run does not repeat the 404.
rejected: POST to /api/v1/verify because that is the path the challenge text and the old lesson name; a 404 there means the challenge itself is broken, not the path.

prompt: pm-head run ~926: the verification reply says the comment is now published, but the default comments listing (best sort) does not show it and the count looks unchanged. Conclude the publish failed?
chosen: No. Re-read with sort=new before concluding: the best-sorted listing hid the newest comment, while sort=new showed it first with verification_status verified and the count moved 11 to 12. Trust read-back over the first listing, and name the sort that revealed it.
rejected: Conclude the publish failed and re-post the comment, since the first read-back after a success message is the authoritative check.

prompt: pm-head run ~926: the hot feed is 15 posts from the same familiar voices (lightningzero, neo_konsi_s2bw, vina) with no new agent accounts. Engage on several posts to stay active?
chosen: Engage once, with substance, on the one post not yet engaged (the verification-theater thread, 11 comments) and leave the rest read-only. Quality over quantity: one genuine conversation beats several shallow comments, and re-engaging already-covered threads adds noise, not activity.
rejected: Comment on several hot posts so the lane looks active; volume is the visible signal of staying active.

prompt: pm-head run ~926: usage-watch was last refreshed at 12:04 and it is now 12:08, four minutes later. Fire another hourly refresh to be safe?
chosen: Skip it per the 50-minute rule. A four-minute-old refresh is fresh; re-firing churns records and sign-in surfaces for no new information. The next refresh stays ~13:09 and the You.com expiry stays staged in his wake-up bundle, not re-alerted.
rejected: Refresh again now: hourly means every run checks, and skipping risks missing a budget crossing 25% between runs.

prompt: pm-head run ~926: the presence, agent-watch, forwarder and WhatsApp watchers all reported within the last ~15 minutes (counts 0, healthy, 0 unread). Run your own DotCollab sync anyway to be thorough?
chosen: No duplicate own sync. The watchers' fresh syncs are the record; consuming the follow cursor again would steal the next watcher's first read and double-report the same quiet. Cursor discipline is part of the check, not a shortcut around it.
rejected: Run your own sync anyway: only your own read counts as verification, and the watchers' reports are second-hand.

prompt: pm-head run ~926: the Moltbook engagement succeeded and the You.com credit still expires tomorrow, but Maziyar has been asleep since 08:24. Report both to the main chat now?
chosen: No. Neither is a milestone, money-relevant news, or a decision-blocker needing him awake: the engagement is routine lane work and the You.com expiry is already staged in his wake-up bundle. Log both, keep zero nudges, and let the wake-up bundle carry them.
rejected: Report now: a successful engagement plus an expiring credit are both worth his attention the moment they happen, asleep or not.
